paragraphs.title: The Ruin and Exile of Moab’s Cities

easy.explanation: The verses describe cities that are spoiled, confounded, taken, and made desolate.
easy.q: What is described concerning Moab’s cities?

easy.explanation: The passage says, “Flee, save your lives.”
easy.q: What are the people of Moab commanded to do?

answers: Chemosh, his priests, and his princes
easy.explanation: Chemosh goes into captivity with his priests and princes.
easy.q: Who goes into captivity with Moab?

answers: Because the cities are being invaded
medium.explanation: The spoiler comes upon every city, and the cities are destroyed or captured.
medium.q: Why are the people of Moab forced to flee?

medium.explanation: The passage presents destruction, followed by fleeing and captivity.
medium.q: Which sequence best describes the events?

answers: The cities will be full of people
The cities will become deserted places
medium.explanation: Desolate cities are empty and without inhabitants.
medium.q: What does “the cities thereof shall be desolate” mean?

answers: Moab’s government and worship were also affected
challenge.explanation: The captivity of the priests and princes shows that both religious and political institutions suffered.
challenge.q: What does the mention of priests and princes show about the extent of the judgment?

answers: It limits the destruction to one place
It emphasizes the wide extent of the destruction
challenge.explanation: The many places named show that the judgment was not local but spread throughout Moab.
challenge.q: How does the repeated naming of cities affect the description?

challenge.explanation: The passage says that the strongholds are also taken or destroyed.
challenge.q: What is the relationship between Moab’s strongholds and its fate?

easy.explanation: Moab has been “at ease from his youth” and settled on his lees.
easy.q: How is Moab described at the beginning of this section?

answers: They will be emptied and their bottles broken
easy.explanation: The Lord says that Moab’s vessels will be emptied and their bottles broken.
easy.q: What will happen to Moab’s vessels?

answers: They will be forced to question their strength
easy.explanation: They ask, “How say ye, We are mighty and strong men for the war?”
easy.q: What will happen to Moab’s mighty men?

answers: Because it had remained undisturbed and had not experienced captivity
Because it had been conquered many times
medium.explanation: The image shows that Moab had remained settled and had not been carried into captivity.
medium.q: Why is Moab compared to wine that has not been poured from vessel to vessel?

answers: Its trust in its works and treasures leads to its capture
medium.explanation: Because Moab trusted in its works and treasures, it would also be taken.
medium.q: How is Moab’s confidence connected with its punishment?

medium.explanation: The wording describes the breaking and destruction of the vessels.
medium.q: What does “break their bottles” mean in context?

answers: Moab retained its character because it had remained undisturbed
challenge.explanation: Moab’s taste and scent remained because it had not undergone the upheaval of captivity.
challenge.q: What does the image of unchanged taste and scent suggest?

answers: Ease and complacency contrasted with ruin
challenge.explanation: Moab had been secure, but it would be emptied, broken, and ashamed.
challenge.q: What is the main contrast in this section?

answers: It changes from honor and strength to captivity and shame
challenge.explanation: Moab loses its cities, confidence, and reputation through judgment.
challenge.q: How is Moab’s loss of status expressed?

answers: The fugitive and the escaped person
easy.explanation: The inhabitant of Aroer is told to ask those who flee and escape what has happened.
easy.q: Who is asked to tell what happened to Moab?

easy.explanation: The passage asks, “How is the strong staff broken, and the beautiful rod!”
easy.q: What happened to Moab’s strong staff?

easy.explanation: Dibon and Nebo are included in the list of judged cities.
easy.q: Which places are named among the punished cities?

answers: He leads the army to victory
medium.explanation: The fugitive serves as a source of news about Moab’s defeat.
medium.q: What is the role of the fugitive in this section?

answers: To emphasize the extent of the judgment
medium.explanation: The list shows that judgment reached throughout the land of Moab.
medium.q: Why are many cities listed one after another?

answers: A symbol of power and honor
medium.explanation: The strong staff and beautiful rod symbolize Moab’s strength, authority, and honor.
medium.q: What does “the beautiful rod” represent in context?

answers: The report causes questioning and astonishment
challenge.explanation: The news prompts the question, “How is the strong staff broken?”
challenge.q: What is the relationship between the fugitive’s report and the listeners’ response?

answers: She is near a route used by fleeing people
challenge.explanation: She is positioned where fugitives pass and can ask them what has happened.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from telling the inhabitant of Aroer to stand by the way and watch?

answers: It shows that even many important centers were affected
It proves that Moab was unharmed
challenge.explanation: The judgment of numerous cities demonstrates the breaking of Moab’s power and pride.
challenge.q: How does the list of cities strengthen the message about Moab’s pride?

easy.explanation: Moab’s loftiness, arrogancy, pride, and haughtiness are emphasized.
easy.q: What characteristic of Moab is revealed in this section?

answers: Moab’s destruction and the loss of its produce
easy.explanation: The prophet mourns Moab, its vineyards, its summer fruits, and its ruined cities.

answers: They are going out to trade
easy.explanation: The passage describes shaved heads, clipped beards, cuttings on the hands, and sackcloth.
easy.q: What condition of the people is described near the end of the section?

answers: It represents the end of joy and harvest
medium.explanation: Wine fails, the winepresses are silent, and the sounds of joy cease.
medium.q: How is the loss of wine related to Moab’s destruction?

answers: Pride stands against ruin and mourning
There is no connection between them
medium.explanation: Moab’s arrogance is rebuked while its suffering and destruction are mourned.
medium.q: What is the contrast between Moab’s pride and the prophet’s lament?

medium.explanation: Lamentation refers to sorrowful mourning and crying over disaster.
medium.q: What does “lamentation” mean in this passage?

answers: He grieves over its destruction even while rebuking it
challenge.explanation: The prophet condemns Moab’s pride but also expresses sorrow for its suffering.
challenge.q: What does the prophet’s lament reveal about his attitude toward Moab?

answers: They damage its joy and prosperity
challenge.explanation: The loss of harvest and wine represents the loss of abundance and celebration.
challenge.q: How are the loss of vineyards and wine connected with Moab’s identity?

answers: A sharp reversal in Moab’s condition
challenge.explanation: The proud nation becomes a place of shame, grief, and mourning.
challenge.q: What does the change from pride to mourning signify?

easy.explanation: The Lord says, “Behold, he shall fly as an eagle.”
easy.q: What is the approaching enemy compared to?

easy.explanation: Kerioth is taken and the strongholds are surprised.
easy.q: What happens to the cities of Moab?

answers: That it will not be judged
That its captivity will be brought again in the latter days
easy.explanation: The passage ends with the promise, “I will bring again the captivity of Moab in the latter days.”
easy.q: What is promised to Moab at the end of the passage?

answers: A succession of dangers and traps
medium.explanation: The phrase presents danger surrounding the inhabitants of Moab.
medium.q: What does “fear, and the pit, and the snare” describe?

answers: He falls into the pit or is caught in the snare
medium.explanation: The verse describes escape from one danger leading to another.
medium.q: What happens to the person who flees from fear?

answers: He will move swiftly toward the target
He will remain in one place
He will sink into the ground
medium.explanation: The eagle image conveys a swift and forceful attack.
medium.q: What does “he shall fly as an eagle” suggest?

answers: Present destruction contrasted with a future promise of restoration
Present peace contrasted with future peace
Present wealth contrasted with past wealth
challenge.explanation: The passage describes capture and destruction but ends with a promise of restored fortunes.
challenge.q: What is the main contrast at the end of the chapter?

challenge.explanation: An eagle swooping down represents a rapid and powerful attack.
challenge.q: What does the eagle image emphasize about the attack?

answers: Attempts to flee from fear still end in pits, snares, and capture
challenge.explanation: The passage describes people fleeing from fear only to fall into another trap and face judgment.
challenge.q: How are fear and capture connected in Moab’s fate?
